svg.aria-label: Diagram of Lambda SnapStart for container images. Initialisation runs once when a version is published, and Lambda takes an encrypted Firecracker MicroVM snapshot of the memory and disk state. Every execution environment then resumes from that one snapshot, so anything created during initialisation is duplicated rather than generated afresh: unique identifiers, secrets, entropy for pseudorandomness, and open network connections. Below, what SnapStart cannot be combined with — provisioned concurrency, EFS, S3 Files, ephemeral storage above 512 MB, and the unpublished dollar-LATEST version — and the cost shape, which is free for Java managed runtimes but carries a per-version caching charge billed for a minimum of three hours plus a per-restore charge otherwise.
svg.title: How one SnapStart snapshot becomes many execution environments, and what that duplicates
svg.text: Initialisation runs once. Everything it produced is then copied.
That is the whole trick, and the whole hazard. Container images now get it too, which matters because they initialise more.
At publish, once
Lambda initialises the function
and takes a Firecracker MicroVM
snapshot of memory and disk.
Encrypted, then cached.
One snapshot
Java 11+, Python 3.12+,
.NET 8+ — now from a
container image up to 10 GB,
as well as from a ZIP.
Every environment, resumed from it
So whatever initialisation created is not created again.
It is duplicated: unique IDs, secrets fetched once, the
entropy behind pseudorandomness, and the state of any
network connection opened before the handler ran.
What it cannot be combined with
• Provisioned concurrency
• Amazon EFS, and Amazon S3 Files
• Ephemeral storage above 512 MB
• The unpublished $LATEST version
A 10 GB image is fine. 512 MB of /tmp is the ceiling.
The cost shape is not the same for every runtime
For Java managed runtimes there is no additional cost.
Otherwise you pay to cache each published version's
snapshot — billed for a minimum of three hours, and for
as long as the version stays active — plus a charge each
time an environment is restored from it.
Old versions nobody deleted keep charging.
Why container images make the uniqueness problem sharper
Teams reach for a container image when initialisation is heavy — a model to load, a framework to warm, a connection pool to build.
That is exactly the initialisation most likely to have created something that was supposed to be unique.
Available in all commercial Regions except Asia Pacific (New Zealand) and Asia Pacific (Taipei).
